**Toprak Razgatlıoğlu** (Turkish pronunciation: [['topɾak 'ɾazgatɫɯ'oːɫu]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Turkish "Help:IPA/Turkish")[motorcycle road racer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_racing "Road racing") who, from 2026, rides for [Prima Pramac Yamaha MotoGP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pramac_Racing "Pramac Racing") in the [MotoGP World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Prix_motorcycle_racing "Grand Prix motorcycle racing").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-1) Razgatlıoğlu holds three Superbike World Championship titles: [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Superbike_World_Championship "2021 Superbike World Championship") with the [Yamaha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamaha_Motor_Company "Yamaha Motor Company") factory Superbike team, ending [Jonathan Rea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Rea "Jonathan Rea")'s six-year reign, [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Superbike_World_Championship "2024 Superbike World Championship") and [2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Superbike_World_Championship "2025 Superbike World Championship") with the [BMW Motorrad WorldSBK Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaun_Muir_Racing "Shaun Muir Racing"), the manufacturer's first two titles. He is the first Turkish Superbike World Champion and the rider with the most wins for both Yamaha and [BMW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW_in_motorsport "BMW in motorsport") in the championship, with 37 and 39 total victories respectively, after winning his first two with [Kawasaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kawasaki_Motors "Kawasaki Motors").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-2)
Razgatlıoğlu is well known for his '[stoppie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoppie "Stoppie")' celebration. He is also known for his dominating record, being called a Superbike equivalent to [Marc Márquez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_M%C3%A1rquez "Marc Márquez"). He joined Pramac Racing for the [2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_MotoGP_World_Championship "2026 MotoGP World Championship") season, the year before the 2027 Regulation change, and became the first MotoGP rider hailing from Turkey. He is the first WSBK rider since [Loris Baz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loris_Baz "Loris Baz") to switch to MotoGP and the first WSBK champion since [Ben Spies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Spies "Ben Spies").
## Early life
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]
Born in [Alanya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alanya "Alanya"), Razgatlıoğlu is the second son of the Turkish stunt motorcyclist Arif Razgatlıoğlu, who was known as "Tek Teker Arif" ("Wheelie Arif"). His father, together with his girlfriend who was riding on the [pillion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pillion "Pillion") seat, died following a [motorcycle accident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traffic_collision "Traffic collision") in [Antalya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antalya "Antalya") on 17 November 2017.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-s1-3)
## Career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]
### Early career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early career")]
Razgatlıoğlu competed in the [Red Bull MotoGP Rookies Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull_MotoGP_Rookies_Cup "Red Bull MotoGP Rookies Cup") in 2013 and 2014, finishing tenth and sixth overall respectively. He finished first in the seventh race of the 2014 season in [Sachsenring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sachsenring "Sachsenring"), Germany.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-4)
Razgatlıoğlu won his debut race in the [European Superstock 600 Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Superstock_600_Championship "European Superstock 600 Championship") on 5 October 2014 at [Magny Cours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magny_Cours "Magny Cours") aboard a [Kawasaki ZX-6R](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kawasaki_ZX-6R "Kawasaki ZX-6R").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-6)
Razgatlıoğlu won the 2015 [European Superstock 600 Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Superstock_600_Championship "European Superstock 600 Championship") aboard a [Kawasaki ZX-6R](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kawasaki_ZX-6R "Kawasaki ZX-6R").
### Superbike World Championship
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Superbike World Championship")]
Razgatlıoğlu was an upcoming performer with Turkish Puccetti Kawasaki racing team from 2018 and was partnered with factory Kawasaki riders [Jonathan Rea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Rea "Jonathan Rea") and [Leon Haslam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leon_Haslam "Leon Haslam") for the 2019 [Suzuka 8 Hours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suzuka_8_Hours "Suzuka 8 Hours"), a track [endurance race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endurance_racing_\(motorsport\)#Motorcycle_endurance_racing "Endurance racing \(motorsport\)"). Due to not being allowed to ride with the other two taking turns throughout the race, Razgatlıoğlu soon left the Kawasaki marque to become a factory Yamaha rider from 2020. He became World Champion in [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Superbike_World_Championship "2021 Superbike World Championship") after finishing second in Race 1 at the [Mandalika International Street Circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandalika_International_Street_Circuit "Mandalika International Street Circuit").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-8)
Under contract to Yamaha in the Superbike class from 2020 until 30 November 2023, Razgatlıoğlu was prevented by Yamaha from testing his 2024 BMW machine at an official test held immediately after the 2023 season-end race at [Jerez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuito_de_Jerez "Circuito de Jerez") in late October/early November, when Jonathan Rea, previously with [Kawasaki Racing Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kawasaki_Racing_Team "Kawasaki Racing Team") and Razgatlıoğlu's direct replacement, was allowed to participate on his new Yamaha.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-motom-9)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Razgatlioglu_in_action%2C_2024.jpg/250px-Razgatlioglu_in_action%2C_2024.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Razgatlioglu_in_action,_2024.jpg)Razgatlıoğlu at Donington Park, 2024
Razgatlıoğlu was offered a test on 22/23 November with [gagging conditions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gag_order "Gag order") attached, but chose to wait until 4 December when out of contract to Yamaha.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-motom-9) He rode the BMW over two days at Portimão,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-10) followed by another test at Jerez.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-11)
#### 2024
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2024")]
[BMW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW "BMW") signed Razgatlıoğlu in 2024 on a two-year deal.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-12) Razgatlıoğlu won his first race at race 1 in [Catalunya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuit_de_Barcelona-Catalunya "Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya"), the first win for BMW since 2013 and his 40th overall.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-13) He would then proceed to win the Superpole race by overtaking [Álvaro Bautista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81lvaro_Bautista "Álvaro Bautista") at the last corner of the final lap.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-14) Razgatlıoğlu scored his first [hat trick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hat-trick "Hat-trick") in [Misano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misano_World_Circuit_Marco_Simoncelli "Misano World Circuit Marco Simoncelli");[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-15) this was followed by further consecutive hat tricks at [Donington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donington_Park "Donington Park"),[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-16) [Most](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autodrom_Most "Autodrom Most")[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-17) and [Portimão](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algarve_International_Circuit "Algarve International Circuit").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-18) Razgatlıoğlu crashed heavily during free practice at [Magny-Cours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuit_de_Nevers_Magny-Cours "Circuit de Nevers Magny-Cours") and was ultimately diagnosed with [pneumothorax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pneumothorax "Pneumothorax"); the session was red-flagged as a result. Razgatlioğlu would ultimately be declared unfit to race.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-19)
Razgatlıoğlu broke the record for most consecutive wins in a season with 13 following his hat trick in Portimão;[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-20) he celebrated breaking the record by imitating a viral pose struck by Olympic silver medalist shooter [Yusuf Dikeç](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yusuf_Dike%C3%A7 "Yusuf Dikeç").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-21)
### MotoGP World Championship
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: MotoGP World Championship")]
#### 2022
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2022")]
In June, Razgatlıoğlu got an opportunity to test a [Yamaha YZR-M1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamaha_YZR-M1 "Yamaha YZR-M1") during a one-day MotoGP private test at the [Motorland Aragón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorland_Arag%C3%B3n "Motorland Aragón") circuit. Razgatlıoğlu completed forty laps during this test. No empirical data was made available from the test, likely owing to the test's confidentiality and press being locked out of the event. He was accompanied by Yamaha test rider [Cal Crutchlow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cal_Crutchlow "Cal Crutchlow") during the test.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-22)
#### 2023
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2023")]
[Yamaha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamaha_Motor_Company "Yamaha Motor Company") officially announced that Razgatlıoğlu would ride the [Yamaha YZR-M1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamaha_YZR-M1 "Yamaha YZR-M1") during the development tests held at the [Jerez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuito_de_Jerez "Circuito de Jerez") circuit in [Andalucía](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andaluc%C3%ADa "Andalucía"), Spain, when he joined [Yamaha MotoGP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamaha_Motor_Racing "Yamaha Motor Racing") test rider [Cal Crutchlow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cal_Crutchlow "Cal Crutchlow") for two days on April 10 and 11. This was the second test on the YZR-M1, following his first ride at [Motorland Aragon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorland_Aragon "Motorland Aragon") in June 2022.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-23)
#### 2026: Prima Pramac Racing
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2026: Prima Pramac Racing")]
On June 10, 2025, Yamaha announced that Razgatlıoğlu will move from World Superbikes to MotoGP in [2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_MotoGP_World_Championship "2026 MotoGP World Championship"), riding for the [Prima Pramac Racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pramac_Racing "Pramac Racing") Team. He became the first Turkish MotoGP rider in history, and will be alongside MotoGP Veteran [Jack Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Miller_\(motorcyclist\) "Jack Miller \(motorcyclist\)").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-25) After sustaining a shoulder injury in [Mandalika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Indonesian_motorcycle_Grand_Prix "2026 Indonesian motorcycle Grand Prix"), Razgatlıoğlu missed the final five races of the season in order to undergo surgery and recover.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-26)
## Personal life
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Personal life")]
Nicknamed El Turco, Razgatlıoğlu is managed by former multiple time WSSP champion [Kenan Sofuoğlu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenan_Sofuo%C4%9Flu "Kenan Sofuoğlu"). He resides in [Sakarya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakarya_Province "Sakarya Province"). Toprak's father used to call him Tek Teker Toprak, but he used to get angry by it because he would say ‘I am a racer, not a stunt rider’.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-Top-27) Toprak's father had a shop with [Atari games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atari_games "Atari games") and at the back was a straight where he used to do stunts as a kid.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-Top-27)
On 10 October 2025, Razgatlıoğlu received his 2021 WorldSBK championship winning bike from [Yamaha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamaha_Motor_Racing "Yamaha Motor Racing") after signing a [MotoGP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MotoGP "MotoGP") contract with them.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toprak_Razgatl%C4%B1o%C4%9Flu#cite_note-28)
